trace_environment: non-GPU c7i.2xlarge, vllm fails after import on missing CUDA but trace is complete
interpretation: For vLLM serving cold-start (import + serve readiness, no weights), only ~17% of container bytes are actually read.
26.6% of openat calls are negative lookups (Python import path-walk via sys.path). FUSE backends should fast-path negative results.
Modal's claim that lazy-load wins are bounded by access ratio is confirmed: theoretical max speedup of ~6x via lazy-pull + targeted prefetch.
Image-bake / EBS prebake transfer ALL 22.85 GB. Lazy-pull + access-set-prefetch could transfer ~3.93 GB. The opportunity is real.
next_step_implications: Spec A: prioritize lazy-load variants (SOCI/Nydus) over EBS prebake. Access set is small enough for lazy to win.
Spec A: include FUSE-tuning variant (Spec E config) since FUSE tunables are the inner-loop.
Bake a `prefetch.txt` per image: ship the touched-file list as image metadata so a snapshotter can prefetch it eagerly.
EBS prebake is still useful for warm-pool prepull (one-time cost amortized across replicas), but for autoscale events lazy wins.
